chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Chur
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶7:** This interior spiritual life that remains implanted within the person where good and evil, truth and falsity, are commingled — for it yearns to be elevated and to return to the heavenly society to which it belongs by its inmost love — yet it perceives and comprehends that there is no open passage through any of the faculties of the internal or external mind. For these faculties are its confinement, which [GAP-1] press upon it from every direction. Indeed, it has no open passage except through Divine Love and Divine Truth themselves, the illuminating principles of the spiritual mind, [GAP-2] which become the state of celestial peace for it. And they become the means by which the interior degrees are opened for it [GAP-3: REVIEW in] the liberation from the natural state, and the spiritual life passes through them into the kingdom of heaven where its kindred affections dwell.

**¶8:** Divine Love and Divine Truth, the illuminating principles of the spiritual mind, have no permanent state of peace among any of the created faculties of the internal person; except in the Divine itself, which has been their own dwelling from eternity.

---

*Note on the structure:* The passage describes the condition of spiritual life trapped in the mixed state of the unregenerate mind. Every faculty — natural and spiritual — is closed by the proprium. Only the Lord's own Love (sun) and Truth (moon), acting as vessels of influx from above, can provide rest and open the interior degrees, allowing that life to pass out of confinement into heaven. ¶8 then states the principle behind this: Divine Good and Divine Truth originate in no created thing, but solely in the Lord's own infinite being — they merely pass *through* the mind's faculties without residing in them.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: This [liv]ing sou[l] that is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow][s a]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [presses upon] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the light-givers of the heavens [ ... / ... ] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
The light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the lan[d] of light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading specifies "press upon it from every direction," and "presses upon" is the natural-register verb of oppressive constraint fitting the Kephalaia's description of the powers confining the soul everywhere.

The editor's "in" is confirmed: "a door that opens for it in the coming forth" correctly denotes the circumstance of liberation, matching the spiritual reading's "in the liberation from the natural state."
